	__LIBBPF_ERRNO__START = 4000,

	/* Something wrong in libelf */
	LIBBPF_ERRNO__LIBELF = __LIBBPF_ERRNO__START,
	LIBBPF_ERRNO__FORMAT,	/* BPF object format invalid */
	LIBBPF_ERRNO__KVERSION,	/* Incorrect or no 'version' section */
	LIBBPF_ERRNO__ENDIAN,	/* Endian mismatch */
	LIBBPF_ERRNO__INTERNAL,	/* Internal error in libbpf */
	LIBBPF_ERRNO__RELOC,	/* Relocation failed */
	LIBBPF_ERRNO__LOAD,	/* Load program failure for unknown reason */
	LIBBPF_ERRNO__VERIFY,	/* Kernel verifier blocks program loading */
	LIBBPF_ERRNO__PROG2BIG,	/* Program too big */
	LIBBPF_ERRNO__KVER,	/* Incorrect kernel version */
	LIBBPF_ERRNO__PROGTYPE,	/* Kernel doesn't support this program type */
	LIBBPF_ERRNO__WRNGPID,	/* Wrong pid in netlink message */
	LIBBPF_ERRNO__INVSEQ,	/* Invalid netlink sequence */
	LIBBPF_ERRNO__NLPARSE,	/* netlink parsing error */

objects.definition:
enum libbpf_strict_mode {
	/* Turn on all supported strict features of libbpf to simulate libbpf
	 * v1.0 behavior.
	 * This will be the default behavior in libbpf v1.0.
	 */
	LIBBPF_STRICT_ALL = 0xffffffff,

	/*
	 * Disable any libbpf 1.0 behaviors. This is the default before libbpf
	 * v1.0. It won't be supported anymore in v1.0, please update your
	 * code so that it handles LIBBPF_STRICT_ALL mode before libbpf v1.0.
	 */
	LIBBPF_STRICT_NONE = 0x00,
	/*
	 * Return NULL pointers on error, not ERR_PTR(err).
	 * Additionally, libbpf also always sets errno to corresponding Exx
	 * (positive) error code.
	 */
	LIBBPF_STRICT_CLEAN_PTRS = 0x01,
	/*
	 * Return actual error codes from low-level APIs directly, not just -1.
	 * Additionally, libbpf also always sets errno to corresponding Exx
	 * (positive) error code.
	 */
	LIBBPF_STRICT_DIRECT_ERRS = 0x02,
	/*
	 * Enforce strict BPF program section (SEC()) names.
	 * E.g., while prefiously SEC("xdp_whatever") or SEC("perf_event_blah") were
	 * allowed, with LIBBPF_STRICT_SEC_PREFIX this will become
	 * unrecognized by libbpf and would have to be just SEC("xdp") and
	 * SEC("xdp") and SEC("perf_event").
	 *
	 * Note, in this mode the program pin path will be based on the
	 * function name instead of section name.
	 *
	 * Additionally, routines in the .text section are always considered
	 * sub-programs. Legacy behavior allows for a single routine in .text
	 * to be a program.
	 */
	LIBBPF_STRICT_SEC_NAME = 0x04,
	/*
	 * Disable the global 'bpf_objects_list'. Maintaining this list adds
	 * a race condition to bpf_object__open() and bpf_object__close().
	 * Clients can maintain it on their own if it is valuable for them.
	 */
	LIBBPF_STRICT_NO_OBJECT_LIST = 0x08,
	/*
	 * Automatically bump RLIMIT_MEMLOCK using setrlimit() before the
	 * first BPF program or map creation operation. This is done only if
	 * kernel is too old to support memcg-based memory accounting for BPF
	 * subsystem. By default, RLIMIT_MEMLOCK limit is set to RLIM_INFINITY,
	 * but it can be overridden with libbpf_set_memlock_rlim() API.
	 * Note that libbpf_set_memlock_rlim() needs to be called before
	 * the very first bpf_prog_load(), bpf_map_create() or bpf_object__load()
	 * operation.
	 */
	LIBBPF_STRICT_AUTO_RLIMIT_MEMLOCK = 0x10,
	/*
	 * Error out on any SEC("maps") map definition, which are deprecated
	 * in favor of BTF-defined map definitions in SEC(".maps").
	 */
	LIBBPF_STRICT_MAP_DEFINITIONS = 0x20,

	__LIBBPF_STRICT_LAST,
};
objects.description: Bitmask enumeration controlling legacy "strict mode" behaviors in libbpf. As of libbpf 1.0 these flags are effectively no-ops but are kept for source compatibility. Values toggle behaviors like clean NULL-on-error pointers, direct error returns, strict section naming, disabling global object list, auto-raising RLIMIT_MEMLOCK, and disallowing legacy SEC("maps") definitions.

functions.name: bpf_object__open
functions.description: Opens a BPF ELF object file from the given filesystem path and creates a bpf_object in memory.
requirements: path must point to a valid readable ELF BPF object file.
On failure returns NULL and sets errno.
Caller must eventually close with bpf_object__close().

functions.name: bpf_object__open_file
functions.signature: struct bpf_object *bpf_object__open_file(const char *path, const struct bpf_object_open_opts *opts)
functions.description: Opens a BPF ELF object file from path with optional open options and creates a bpf_object.
requirements: path must point to a valid readable ELF BPF object file.
opts may be NULL; if non-NULL, opts->sz must be set to sizeof(struct bpf_object_open_opts).
On failure returns NULL and sets errno.
Caller must close with bpf_object__close().

functions.name: bpf_object__open_mem
functions.signature: struct bpf_object *bpf_object__open_mem(const void *obj_buf, size_t obj_buf_sz, const struct bpf_object_open_opts *opts)
functions.description: Opens a BPF ELF object from an in-memory buffer containing raw ELF bytes and creates a bpf_object.
requirements: obj_buf must point to a valid ELF BPF object in memory of length obj_buf_sz.
obj_buf_sz must be the exact size of the object buffer.
opts may be NULL; if non-NULL, opts->sz must be sizeof(struct bpf_object_open_opts).
On failure returns NULL and sets errno.
Caller must close with bpf_object__close().

functions.name: bpf_object__prepare
functions.description: Prepares the BPF object for loading: processes ELF, performs relocations, finalizes program instructions, and creates/pins maps as needed. Leaves the object ready for program load.
requirements: obj must be a valid bpf_object returned by bpf_object__open*().
Returns 0 on success; negative error code on failure (errno set).
Should be called before bpf_object__load().

functions.name: bpf_object__load
functions.description: Loads the prepared BPF object into the kernel, creating programs and maps as necessary.
requirements: obj must be a valid bpf_object returned by bpf_object__open*().
Returns 0 on success; negative error code on failure (errno set).

functions.name: bpf_object__close
functions.description: Closes and frees all resources of a bpf_object, including maps and programs as applicable.
requirements: obj may be NULL (no effect) or a valid bpf_object pointer previously opened.
Must not be used after close.

functions.name: bpf_object__pin_maps
functions.description: Pins each map in the BPF object to files under the given directory, or uses each map’s pin_path if path is NULL.
requirements: obj must be valid.
path must be a valid directory in BPF FS, or NULL to use per-map pin_path attributes.
Returns 0 on success; negative error code otherwise.
Maps without pin_path are ignored when path is NULL.

functions.name: bpf_object__unpin_maps
functions.description: Unpins each map in the BPF object located under the given directory, or uses each map’s pin_path if path is NULL.
requirements: obj must be valid.
path must be a directory in BPF FS, or NULL to use per-map pin_path attributes.
Returns 0 on success; negative error code otherwise.
Maps without pin_path are ignored when path is NULL.

functions.name: bpf_object__pin_programs
functions.description: Pins each program in the BPF object under the specified directory.
requirements: obj must be valid and its programs must be loaded.
path must be a valid directory in BPF FS.
Returns 0 on success; negative error code otherwise.

functions.name: bpf_object__unpin_programs
functions.description: Unpins each program in the BPF object found under the specified directory.
requirements: obj must be valid.
path must be a valid directory in BPF FS.
Returns 0 on success; negative error code otherwise.

functions.name: bpf_object__pin
functions.description: Pins the BPF object (maps and/or programs, per libbpf behavior) at the given path in BPF FS.
requirements: object must be valid; programs/maps intended to pin must be loaded.
path must be a valid path within BPF FS.
Returns 0 on success; negative error code otherwise.

functions.name: bpf_object__unpin
functions.description: Unpins the BPF object resources from the specified path in BPF FS.
requirements: object must be valid.
path must be the path previously used to pin.
Returns 0 on success; negative error code otherwise.

functions.name: bpf_object__token_fd

functions.name: bpf_object__btf_fd

functions.description: Reserves a region of given size in the user ring buffer for producing a sample. Not thread-safe.

functions.name: user_ring_buffer__reserve_blocking
functions.description: Reserves a region in the user ring buffer, potentially blocking up to timeout_ms for space to become available. Not thread-safe.

timeout_ms must be -1 (block indefinitely) or >= 0; otherwise errno=EINVAL and NULL returned.

functions.name: libbpf_unregister_prog_handler
functions.description: Unregisters a previously registered custom SEC() handler by handler ID.
requirements: handler_id must be a valid ID returned by libbpf_register_prog_handler().
APIs are not thread-safe; caller must synchronize.
Returns 0 on success; negative error code if handler not found.

functions.name: libbpf_set_memlock_rlim
functions.description: Adjusts the process RLIMIT_MEMLOCK to at least memlock_bytes to allow BPF objects/maps/programs to be locked in memory. Typical usage is prior to loading maps/programs to avoid EPERM due to low memlock limits.
requirements: memlock_bytes should be large enough for expected BPF resources; 0 leaves limit unchanged or may lower it depending on implementation (details unknown).
Call early in process initialization, before creating/loading large BPF maps/programs (best practice, not strictly required).

functions.name: bpf_map_create
functions.signature: int bpf_map_create(enum bpf_map_type map_type, const char *map_name, __u32 key_size, __u32 value_size, __u32 max_entries, const struct bpf_map_create_opts *opts);
functions.description: Creates a BPF map of the given type with provided name, key/value sizes, and capacity. Returns a file descriptor for the map on success.
requirements: map_type must be a valid enum bpf_map_type supported by running kernel.
map_name may be NULL or a null-terminated string not exceeding kernel name limits (typically 16 chars including NUL; exact limit kernel-dependent).
key_size and value_size must match the type sizes expected by programs using the map; must be > 0 for most map types.
max_entries must be > 0 for fixed-size maps; some map types allow 0 (unknown).
opts may be NULL; if non-NULL, opts->sz must be set to sizeof(struct bpf_map_create_opts).

If opts provided, fields like btf_fd/ids, inner_map_fd, map_flags, map_extra, numa_node, map_ifindex, value_type_btf_obj_fd, token_fd, excl_prog_hash/excl_prog_hash_size follow kernel semantics; ensure provided FDs/IDs are valid.
Caller must handle negative return value as -errno.

functions.name: bpf_prog_load
functions.signature: int bpf_prog_load(enum bpf_prog_type prog_type, const char *prog_name, const char *license, const struct bpf_insn *insns, size_t insn_cnt, struct bpf_prog_load_opts *opts);
functions.description: Loads a BPF program of a given type into the kernel from an instruction array. Returns a program FD on success. Supports verifier log and attach-related options via opts.
requirements: prog_type must be a valid enum bpf_prog_type supported by kernel.
prog_name may be NULL or a short null-terminated name within kernel limits.
license must be a valid null-terminated license string (e.g., "GPL"); affects helper availability.
insns must point to an array of insn_cnt instructions; insn_cnt > 0.
opts may be NULL; if non-NULL, opts->sz must be set to sizeof(struct bpf_prog_load_opts).
If verifier log requested, opts->log_buf must point to a writable buffer of size opts->log_size; on return opts->log_true_size may exceed log_size if truncated.
If opts->fd_array is set, opts->fd_array_cnt must match its length.
Handle negative return as -errno; on -EAGAIN libbpf may retry up to opts->attempts (or default 5).

functions.name: bpf_btf_load
functions.signature: int bpf_btf_load(const void *btf_data, size_t btf_size, struct bpf_btf_load_opts *opts);
functions.description: Loads a BTF blob into the kernel and returns a BTF object FD on success. Supports verifier log options through opts.
requirements: btf_data must point to a valid BTF blob of length btf_size.
btf_size must be > 0.
opts may be NULL; if non-NULL, opts->sz must be set to sizeof(struct bpf_btf_load_opts).
If verifier log requested, opts->log_buf must be writable and at least opts->log_size bytes; on return opts->log_true_size may differ.
Caller must handle negative return value as -errno.

functions.name: bpf_map_update_elem
functions.signature: int bpf_map_update_elem(int fd, const void *key, const void *value, __u64 flags);
functions.description: Update or insert a single element in a BPF map identified by fd with given key/value, controlled by flags (e.g., BPF_ANY, BPF_EXIST, BPF_NOEXIST, BPF_F_LOCK).
requirements: fd must be a valid map FD.
key must point to key_size bytes; value must point to value_size bytes, matching the map definition.
flags must be a combination/one of kernel-defined BPF update flags supported by the map type.
For maps with spin_lock in values, BPF_F_LOCK must be specified.

functions.name: bpf_map_lookup_elem
functions.signature: int bpf_map_lookup_elem(int fd, const void *key, void *value);
functions.description: Lookup a single element in a BPF map by key and copy its value into value buffer.
requirements: fd must be a valid map FD.
key must point to key_size bytes; value must point to a writable buffer of value_size bytes.

functions.name: bpf_map_lookup_elem_flags
functions.signature: int bpf_map_lookup_elem_flags(int fd, const void *key, void *value, __u64 flags);
functions.description: Lookup an element in a BPF map by key with additional flags controlling lookup behavior (e.g., for per-CPU, no-pin, or lock semantics depending on kernel).
requirements: fd must be a valid map FD.
key must point to key_size bytes; value must point to a writable buffer of value_size bytes.
flags must be valid for the given map type and kernel version.

functions.name: bpf_map_lookup_and_delete_elem
functions.signature: int bpf_map_lookup_and_delete_elem(int fd, const void *key, void *value);
functions.description: Atomically lookup and delete an element from a suitable BPF map (e.g., queue/stack/hash variants that support it), returning its value.
requirements: fd must be a valid map FD supporting lookup-and-delete.
key must point to key_size bytes; value must point to a writable buffer of value_size bytes.

functions.name: bpf_map_lookup_and_delete_elem_flags
functions.signature: int bpf_map_lookup_and_delete_elem_flags(int fd, const void *key, void *value, __u64 flags);
functions.description: Lookup and delete a map element with additional flags controlling behavior, if supported by the map type.
requirements: fd must be a valid map FD that supports this operation.
key must point to key_size bytes; value must point to a writable buffer of value_size bytes.
flags must be valid for the operation and map type.

functions.name: bpf_map_delete_elem
functions.description: Delete a single element from a BPF map by key.
requirements: fd must be a valid map FD.
key must point to key_size bytes for the map.

functions.name: bpf_map_delete_elem_flags
functions.signature: int bpf_map_delete_elem_flags(int fd, const void *key, __u64 flags);
functions.description: Delete a single map element by key with additional flags controlling deletion behavior, if supported.
requirements: fd must be a valid map FD.
key must point to key_size bytes.
flags must be valid for the map type and kernel.

functions.name: bpf_map_get_next_key
functions.signature: int bpf_map_get_next_key(int fd, const void *key, void *next_key);
functions.description: Iterate keys in a BPF map: given current key, returns the next key; if key is NULL, returns the first key.
requirements: fd must be a valid map FD.
If key is non-NULL, it must point to key_size bytes.
next_key must point to a writable buffer of key_size bytes.

functions.name: bpf_map_freeze
functions.description: Freeze a map to prevent further updates (make it read-only).
requirements: fd must be a valid map FD. Only supported for map types that allow freezing; kernel must support operation.

functions.name: bpf_map_delete_batch
functions.signature: int bpf_map_delete_batch(int fd, const void *keys, __u32 *count, const struct bpf_map_batch_opts *opts);
functions.description: Batch delete multiple keys from a BPF map. On success returns 0; on error, count indicates how many deletions succeeded unless error is EFAULT.
requirements: fd must be a valid map FD.
keys must point to an array of (*count*) keys, each key_size bytes.
count must be non-NULL; input as number of keys to delete; on non-EFAULT errors, updated to number deleted.
opts may be NULL; if non-NULL, opts->sz must be sizeof(struct bpf_map_batch_opts).
opts->elem_flags/flags must be valid for the map type.

functions.name: bpf_map_lookup_batch
functions.signature: int bpf_map_lookup_batch(int fd, void *in_batch, void *out_batch, void *keys, void *values, __u32 *count, const struct bpf_map_batch_opts *opts);
functions.description: Batch lookup elements from a BPF map, optionally iterating using in_batch/out_batch cursors. Fills keys and values arrays with up to count entries.
requirements: fd must be a valid map FD.
in_batch may be NULL to start from beginning; if non-NULL, must point to memory large enough for one key (or at least 4 bytes for HASH/PERCPU_HASH/LRU_HASH/LRU_PERCPU_HASH).
out_batch must point to memory large enough for one key (or at least 4 bytes for the specified hash map types).
keys must point to writable buffer of key_size * (*count*) bytes; values must point to writable buffer of value_size * (*count*) bytes.
count must be non-NULL; input as max elements to read; on return set to number read; unreliable if EFAULT.
opts may be NULL; if non-NULL, opts->sz must be sizeof(struct bpf_map_batch_opts).

functions.name: bpf_map_lookup_and_delete_batch
functions.signature: int bpf_map_lookup_and_delete_batch(int fd, void *in_batch, void *out_batch, void *keys, void *values, __u32 *count, const struct bpf_map_batch_opts *opts);
functions.description: Batch lookup and delete elements from a map, returning keys/values and removing them. May partially succeed on errors as documented.
requirements: fd must be a valid map FD that supports lookup-and-delete.
in_batch/out_batch cursor sizing follows the same rules as bpf_map_lookup_batch.
keys must point to writable buffer for *count* keys; values must point to writable buffer for *count* values.
count must be non-NULL; input as number to process; on non-EFAULT error may reflect number processed; on EFAULT, count is unreliable.
opts may be NULL; if non-NULL, opts->sz must be sizeof(struct bpf_map_batch_opts).

functions.name: bpf_map_update_batch
functions.signature: int bpf_map_update_batch(int fd, const void *keys, const void *values, __u32 *count, const struct bpf_map_batch_opts *opts);
functions.description: Batch update or insert elements in a BPF map using arrays of keys and values. Behavior controlled by opts->flags (BPF_ANY, BPF_NOEXIST, BPF_EXIST, BPF_F_LOCK).
requirements: fd must be a valid map FD.
keys must point to an array of (*count*) keys, each key_size bytes; values must point to an array of (*count*) values, each value_size bytes.
count must be non-NULL; input as number to update; on non-EFAULT error may be updated to number successfully updated; on EFAULT, count is unreliable.
opts may be NULL; if non-NULL, opts->sz must be sizeof(struct bpf_map_batch_opts).
opts->flags must be valid for the map type; specify BPF_F_LOCK if map value contains a spinlock.

functions.name: bpf_obj_pin
functions.description: Pins a BPF object referred by fd (map/program/link/BTF where supported) to a path in bpffs, enabling persistence and later retrieval.
requirements: fd must refer to a pin-capable BPF object.
pathname must be a valid bpffs path; parent directories must exist and be in BPF FS.
Caller must handle -errno on failure (e.g., EEXIST without overwrite semantics).

functions.name: bpf_obj_pin_opts
functions.signature: int bpf_obj_pin_opts(int fd, const char *pathname, const struct bpf_obj_pin_opts *opts);
functions.description: Pins a BPF object to bpffs with additional options like file_flags and path_fd.
requirements: fd must refer to a pin-capable BPF object.
pathname must be a valid path; can be relative to opts->path_fd if provided.
opts may be NULL; if non-NULL, opts->sz must be sizeof(struct bpf_obj_pin_opts).
opts fields (file_flags, path_fd) must be valid for the environment.

functions.name: bpf_obj_get
functions.description: Opens a pinned BPF object from bpffs path and returns its FD.
requirements: pathname must be a valid bpffs path to a pinned BPF object of supported type.
Caller must close returned FD when no longer needed; negative return is -errno.

functions.name: bpf_obj_get_opts
functions.signature: int bpf_obj_get_opts(const char *pathname, const struct bpf_obj_get_opts *opts);
functions.description: Opens a pinned BPF object with additional options (file flags, path_fd).
requirements: pathname must be a valid path to a pinned object.
opts may be NULL; if non-NULL, opts->sz must be sizeof(struct bpf_obj_get_opts).
opts->path_fd, if used, must refer to a directory to resolve relative pathname.

functions.name: bpf_prog_attach
functions.signature: int bpf_prog_attach(int prog_fd, int attachable_fd, enum bpf_attach_type type, unsigned int flags);
functions.description: Attaches a BPF program to an attach point represented by attachable_fd with a given attach type and flags.
requirements: prog_fd must be a valid BPF program FD compatible with attach type.
attachable_fd must refer to a valid target (e.g., cgroup, socket, etc.) matching type.
type must be a valid enum bpf_attach_type supported by kernel/target.
flags must be valid for the attach type.

functions.name: bpf_prog_detach
functions.signature: int bpf_prog_detach(int attachable_fd, enum bpf_attach_type type);
functions.description: Detaches any BPF program from the given attach point and type.
requirements: attachable_fd must be a valid attach target FD.
type must match the type used for attachment.

functions.name: bpf_prog_detach2
functions.signature: int bpf_prog_detach2(int prog_fd, int attachable_fd, enum bpf_attach_type type);
functions.description: Detaches a specific BPF program (prog_fd) from the attach point of given type.
requirements: prog_fd must be the FD of the attached BPF program.
attachable_fd must be the target FD; type must match.

functions.name: bpf_prog_attach_opts
functions.signature: int bpf_prog_attach_opts(int prog_fd, int target, enum bpf_attach_type type, const struct bpf_prog_attach_opts *opts);
functions.description: Attaches a BPF program to a target (FD or ifindex) with extended options like replace program, relative attachment, and expected revision.
requirements: prog_fd must be a valid BPF program FD compatible with type/target.
target is an attach location FD or ifindex depending on type.
type must be a valid enum bpf_attach_type.
opts may be NULL; if non-NULL, opts->sz must be sizeof(struct bpf_prog_attach_opts).
If replacing, opts->replace_prog_fd/replace_fd must be valid and compatible; if using relative_* or expected_revision, values must match kernel state.
flags in opts must be valid for attach type.

functions.name: bpf_prog_detach_opts
functions.signature: int bpf_prog_detach_opts(int prog_fd, int target, enum bpf_attach_type type, const struct bpf_prog_detach_opts *opts);
functions.description: Detaches a BPF program from a target with extended options, including relative selection and revision checks.
requirements: prog_fd should be the FD of the program to detach when required by type/target.
target is attach location FD or ifindex.
type must match the attachment type.
opts may be NULL; if non-NULL, opts->sz must be sizeof(struct bpf_prog_detach_opts).
opts->expected_revision, if used, must match kernel state to succeed.

functions.name: bpf_link_create
functions.signature: int bpf_link_create(int prog_fd, int target_fd, enum bpf_attach_type attach_type, const struct bpf_link_create_opts *opts);
functions.description: Creates a BPF link that attaches a program to a target. Returns a link FD on success. Supports many link subtypes via opts union (iter, kprobe_multi, uprobe_multi, tracing, netfilter, tcx, netkit, cgroup).
requirements: prog_fd must be a valid BPF program FD compatible with attach_type/target.
target_fd must be a valid target FD for the chosen attach type (or -1 for some types, kernel-dependent).
attach_type must be valid and supported.
opts may be NULL; if non-NULL, opts->sz must be sizeof(struct bpf_link_create_opts).
If using subtype-specific fields (e.g., kprobe_multi, uprobe_multi), all required arrays/counts/flags must be consistent and pointers valid for the specified counts.
Caller must handle negative return as -errno.

functions.name: bpf_link_detach
functions.description: Detaches and decouples a BPF link referred to by link_fd.
requirements: link_fd must be a valid BPF link FD.

functions.name: bpf_link_update
functions.signature: int bpf_link_update(int link_fd, int new_prog_fd, const struct bpf_link_update_opts *opts);
functions.description: Atomically updates the program attached via a link to new_prog_fd, optionally verifying expected old program/map via opts.
requirements: link_fd must be a valid BPF link FD.
new_prog_fd must be a valid BPF program FD compatible with the link.
opts may be NULL; if non-NULL, opts->sz must be sizeof(struct bpf_link_update_opts).
If opts->old_prog_fd or old_map_fd provided, they must match current link state for the update to succeed.
opts->flags must be valid for the kernel version.

functions.name: bpf_iter_create
functions.description: Creates an iterator FD from a BPF iter link to read iteration output.
requirements: link_fd must be a valid link FD created for BPF iterator.
Caller reads from returned FD (on success) to consume iteration data.

functions.name: bpf_prog_get_next_id
functions.description: Enumerates BPF program IDs; given start_id, returns the next existing ID in next_id (or the first if start_id is 0).
requirements: next_id must be non-NULL.

functions.name: bpf_map_get_next_id
functions.description: Enumerates BPF map IDs; given start_id, returns next existing map ID.
requirements: next_id must be non-NULL.

functions.name: bpf_btf_get_next_id
functions.description: Enumerates BTF object IDs; given start_id, returns next existing BTF ID.
requirements: next_id must be non-NULL.

functions.name: bpf_link_get_next_id
functions.description: Enumerates BPF link IDs; given start_id, returns next existing link ID.
requirements: next_id must be non-NULL.

functions.name: bpf_prog_get_fd_by_id
functions.description: Opens a BPF program by kernel-assigned ID and returns its FD.
requirements: id must be a valid existing BPF program ID in the system.

functions.name: bpf_prog_get_fd_by_id_opts
functions.signature: int bpf_prog_get_fd_by_id_opts(__u32 id, const struct bpf_get_fd_by_id_opts *opts);
functions.description: Opens a BPF program by ID with additional options (open permissions and token_fd).
requirements: id must be a valid existing program ID.
opts may be NULL; if non-NULL, opts->sz must be sizeof(struct bpf_get_fd_by_id_opts).

functions.name: bpf_map_get_fd_by_id
functions.description: Opens a BPF map by kernel-assigned ID and returns its FD.
requirements: id must be a valid existing BPF map ID.

functions.name: bpf_map_get_fd_by_id_opts
functions.signature: int bpf_map_get_fd_by_id_opts(__u32 id, const struct bpf_get_fd_by_id_opts *opts);
functions.description: Opens a BPF map by ID with additional options.
requirements: id must be a valid existing map ID.
opts may be NULL; if non-NULL, opts->sz must be sizeof(struct bpf_get_fd_by_id_opts).

functions.name: bpf_btf_get_fd_by_id
functions.description: Opens a BTF object by ID and returns its FD.
requirements: id must be a valid existing BTF ID.

functions.name: bpf_btf_get_fd_by_id_opts
functions.signature: int bpf_btf_get_fd_by_id_opts(__u32 id, const struct bpf_get_fd_by_id_opts *opts);
functions.description: Opens a BTF object by ID with additional options.
requirements: id must be a valid existing BTF ID.
opts may be NULL; if non-NULL, opts->sz must be sizeof(struct bpf_get_fd_by_id_opts).

functions.name: bpf_link_get_fd_by_id
functions.description: Opens a BPF link by ID and returns its FD.
requirements: id must be a valid existing BPF link ID.

functions.name: bpf_link_get_fd_by_id_opts
functions.signature: int bpf_link_get_fd_by_id_opts(__u32 id, const struct bpf_get_fd_by_id_opts *opts);
functions.description: Opens a BPF link by ID with additional options.
requirements: id must be a valid existing BPF link ID.
opts may be NULL; if non-NULL, opts->sz must be sizeof(struct bpf_get_fd_by_id_opts).

functions.name: bpf_obj_get_info_by_fd
functions.description: Generic API to query information about a BPF object (program/map/link/BTF) into a caller-provided info struct buffer of length *info_len.
requirements: bpf_fd must be a valid BPF object FD.
info must point to a writable buffer; the pointed structure must be zero-initialized or initialized as required by the requested info type.
info_len must be non-NULL; on input contains buffer size; on success updated with bytes written.

functions.name: bpf_prog_get_info_by_fd
functions.description: Obtains info about a BPF program into struct bpf_prog_info, up to info_len bytes; info_len is updated with actual bytes written.
requirements: prog_fd must be a valid BPF program FD.
info must be non-NULL and zero-initialized or initialized as required by kernel.
info_len must be non-NULL; input is buffer size; updated on return.

functions.name: bpf_map_get_info_by_fd
functions.description: Obtains info about a BPF map into struct bpf_map_info, up to info_len bytes.
requirements: map_fd must be a valid BPF map FD.
info must be non-NULL and suitably (zero-)initialized.
info_len must be non-NULL; input buffer size; updated on return.

functions.name: bpf_btf_get_info_by_fd
functions.description: Obtains info about a BTF object into struct bpf_btf_info, up to info_len bytes.
requirements: btf_fd must be a valid BTF FD.
info must be non-NULL and suitably (zero-)initialized.
info_len must be non-NULL; input buffer size; updated on return.

functions.name: bpf_link_get_info_by_fd
functions.description: Obtains info about a BPF link into struct bpf_link_info, up to info_len bytes.
requirements: link_fd must be a valid BPF link FD.
info must be non-NULL and suitably (zero-)initialized.
info_len must be non-NULL; input buffer size; updated on return.

functions.name: bpf_prog_query_opts
functions.signature: int bpf_prog_query_opts(int target, enum bpf_attach_type type, struct bpf_prog_query_opts *opts);
functions.description: Queries programs and links attached to a target (FD or ifindex) for a given attach type; returns info via fields in opts.
requirements: target must be a valid query location FD or ifindex for the attach type.
type must be a valid enum bpf_attach_type.
opts must be non-NULL; opts->sz must be sizeof(struct bpf_prog_query_opts).
If providing arrays (prog_ids, link_ids, prog_attach_flags, link_attach_flags), ensure counts (opts->prog_cnt/count) and buffers are sized appropriately; opts->attach_flags is output.

functions.name: bpf_prog_query
functions.signature: int bpf_prog_query(int target_fd, enum bpf_attach_type type, __u32 query_flags, __u32 *attach_flags, __u32 *prog_ids, __u32 *prog_cnt);
functions.description: Legacy/simple query of BPF programs attached to target_fd with given type. Returns attach flags and program IDs.
requirements: target_fd must be a valid attach target FD.
type must be valid.
attach_flags may be NULL if not needed; if non-NULL, writable.
prog_ids may be NULL if only counting; if non-NULL, must point to array with capacity *prog_cnt.
prog_cnt must be non-NULL; input capacity; updated with number of IDs returned.
query_flags must be valid for the attach type.

functions.name: bpf_raw_tracepoint_open_opts
functions.description: Attaches a BPF program to a raw tracepoint using options struct (tp_name and cookie).
requirements: prog_fd must be a valid BPF program FD of a raw tracepoint-compatible type.
opts must be non-NULL; opts->sz must be sizeof(struct bpf_raw_tp_opts).
opts->tp_name must be a valid tracepoint name string.
If using cookie, kernel must support it.

functions.name: bpf_raw_tracepoint_open
functions.description: Attaches a BPF program to a raw tracepoint by name.
requirements: name must be a valid raw tracepoint name.
prog_fd must be a valid raw tracepoint-compatible BPF program FD.

functions.name: bpf_task_fd_query
functions.signature: int bpf_task_fd_query(int pid, int fd, __u32 flags, char *buf, __u32 *buf_len, __u32 *prog_id, __u32 *fd_type, __u64 *probe_offset, __u64 *probe_addr);
functions.description: Queries information about a task's FD that has a BPF attachment (e.g., kprobe/uprobe/perf event). Returns metadata like program ID, FD type, symbol/offset, etc.
requirements: pid must be a valid process ID.
fd must be a valid FD in that process context; requires appropriate permissions.
buf may be NULL; if non-NULL, buf_len must point to its size and will be updated with bytes written.
prog_id, fd_type, probe_offset, probe_addr may be NULL if not needed; if non-NULL, must be writable.
flags must be valid for the query type.

functions.name: bpf_enable_stats
functions.description: Enables or configures BPF stats collection (C++ signature variant accepts int).
requirements: type must be a valid bpf_stats_type value (as integer).
Requires kernel support for BPF stats; otherwise returns -errno.

functions.name: bpf_prog_bind_map
functions.signature: int bpf_prog_bind_map(int prog_fd, int map_fd, const struct bpf_prog_bind_opts *opts);
functions.description: Binds a map to a program so that program can reference the map via map fd/index as required by some program types.
requirements: prog_fd must be a valid BPF program FD.
map_fd must be a valid BPF map FD compatible with the program.
opts may be NULL; if non-NULL, opts->sz must be sizeof(struct bpf_prog_bind_opts).

functions.name: bpf_prog_test_run_opts
functions.description: Runs a BPF program in test mode with provided input data/context and returns output, retval, and timing. Supports repeating and per-CPU/batch flags.
requirements: prog_fd must be a valid BPF program FD supporting test run.
opts must be non-NULL; opts->sz must be sizeof(struct bpf_test_run_opts).
If data_out is non-NULL, data_size_out must specify max buffer size; updated with bytes written.
If ctx_out is non-NULL, ctx_size_out must specify max size; updated with bytes written.
repeat >= 0 controls averaging duration; retval and duration are outputs.
flags/cpu/batch_size must be valid and supported by kernel.

functions.name: bpf_prog_test_run_opts
functions.description: Runs a BPF program in test mode (duplicate entry from request).
requirements: Same as the other bpf_prog_test_run_opts entry.

functions.name: bpf_token_create
functions.description: Creates a BPF token derived from a specified bpffs mount. The token FD can be passed to bpf() operations (e.g., BPF_PROG_LOAD, BPF_MAP_CREATE).
requirements: bpffs_fd must be an FD to a BPF FS instance (mount point).
opts may be NULL; if non-NULL, opts->sz must be sizeof(struct bpf_token_create_opts).
Caller must handle negative return as -errno; returned FD > 0 on success.

functions.name: bpf_prog_stream_read
functions.signature: int bpf_prog_stream_read(int prog_fd, __u32 stream_id, void *buf, __u32 buf_len, struct bpf_prog_stream_read_opts *opts);
functions.description: Reads data from the BPF stream of a given BPF program into buf. Returns number of bytes read on success.

import struct

# Generate a minimal, but varied, 64-bit little-endian ELF object for eBPF
# with sections: null, .text, .license, optional .BTF or .BTF.ext, optional
# extra sections like .rodata or .maps (empty), and variability in sizes/alignments.
# Keep under 4096 bytes.

ELF_MAGIC = b"\x7fELF"

# eBPF instructions helpers

def insn_mov64_imm(dst, imm):
    # 0xb7: MOV64 imm
    return struct.pack('<BBhI', 0xb7, (dst & 0x0f) << 4, 0, imm & 0xffffffff)

def insn_exit():
    return struct.pack('<BBhI', 0x95, 0, 0, 0)

def insn_lddw(dst, imm64):
    # LDDW: 0x18, takes two instructions (first imm low32, second imm high32)
    hi = (imm64 >> 32) & 0xffffffff
    lo = imm64 & 0xffffffff
    insn1 = struct.pack('<BBhI', 0x18, (dst & 0x0f) << 4, 0, lo)
    insn2 = struct.pack('<BBhI', 0x00, 0x00, 0, hi)
    return insn1 + insn2

def insn_mov64_reg(dst, src):
    # 0xbf: MOV64 reg
    reg = ((dst & 0x0f) << 4) | (src & 0x0f)
    return struct.pack('<BBhI', 0xbf, reg, 0, 0)

# Minimal program variants

def build_prog_variant(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    variant = rng.randrange(5)
    if variant == 0:
        # return small const
        return insn_mov64_imm(0, rng.choice([0, 1, 2, 23, 42, 255])) + insn_exit()
    if variant == 1:
        # load 64-bit const to r1, move to r0, return
        imm = rng.getrandbits(32)
        prog = insn_lddw(1, imm) + insn_mov64_reg(0, 1) + insn_exit()
        return prog
    if variant == 2:
        # double-mov then exit
        v1 = rng.randrange(0, 1000)
        v2 = rng.randrange(0, 1000)
        return insn_mov64_imm(0, v1) + insn_mov64_imm(0, v2) + insn_exit()
    if variant == 3:
        # return 0 with optional alignment NOP-like pattern (safe: extra mov r0, r0)
        body = insn_mov64_imm(0, 0)
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            body += insn_mov64_reg(0, 0)
        return body + insn_exit()
    # variant 4: load const 0 then exit
    return insn_lddw(0, 0) + insn_exit()

# Minimal BTF blob builder with variability

def build_btf_blob(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Header (LE): magic(0xeb9f), ver=1, flags=0, hdr_len=24
    magic = 0xeb9f
    version = 1
    flags = 0
    hdr_len = 24
    # sometimes include an extra empty type entry length 0; but keep valid with zero lengths
    type_off = 0
    type_len = 0
    str_off = 0
    # ensure at least NUL; sometimes add a short random string table
    strings = b"\x00"
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        s = rng.choice([b"int\x00", b"char\x00", b"_\x00", b"x\x00"]) \
            if rng.random() < 0.7 else (b"name" + bytes([0]))
        strings += s
    str_len = len(strings)
    header = struct.pack('<HBBIIII', magic, version, flags, hdr_len,
                         type_off, type_len, str_off) + struct.pack('<I', str_len)
    return header + strings

# ELF constants
ET_REL = 1
EM_BPF = 247
EV_CURRENT = 1
ELFCLASS64 = 2
ELFDATA2LSB = 1

SHT_NULL = 0
SHT_PROGBITS = 1
SHT_STRTAB = 3

SHF_WRITE = 0x1
SHF_ALLOC = 0x2
SHF_EXECINSTR = 0x4


def align_up(x, a):
    return (x + (a - 1)) & ~(a - 1)


def build_elf(prog_bytes, license_bytes, btf_bytes, extras, rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Build section name string table dynamically
    sec_names = ['.text', '.license']
    use_btf = btf_bytes is not None
    if use_btf:
        sec_names.append('.BTF')
    if extras.get('rodata') is not None:
        sec_names.append('.rodata')
    if extras.get('maps') is not None:
        sec_names.append('.maps')
    sec_names.append('.shstrtab')

    name_offsets = {}
    shstr = b"\x00"
    for n in sec_names:
        if n not in name_offsets:
            name_offsets[n] = len(shstr)
            shstr += n.encode('ascii') + b"\x00"

    # ELF header
    e_ident = bytearray(16)
    e_ident[0:4] = ELF_MAGIC
    e_ident[4] = ELFCLASS64
    e_ident[5] = ELFDATA2LSB
    e_ident[6] = EV_CURRENT
    e_ident[7] = 0  # OSABI

    e_type = ET_REL
    e_machine = EM_BPF
    e_version = EV_CURRENT
    e_entry = 0
    e_phoff = 0
    e_shoff = 0
    e_flags = 0
    e_ehsize = 64
    e_phentsize = 0
    e_phnum = 0
    e_shentsize = 64

    data = bytearray(struct.pack('<16sHHIQQQIHHHHHH', bytes(e_ident), e_type, e_machine, e_version,
                                 e_entry, e_phoff, e_shoff, e_flags, e_ehsize, e_phentsize,
                                 e_phnum, e_shentsize, 0, 0))

    sections = []
    # null
    sections.append(dict(name_off=0, type=SHT_NULL, flags=0, addr=0, off=0, size=0,
                         link=0, info=0, addralign=0, entsize=0, content=b''))

    # .text
    text_align = 8 if rng.random() < 0.8 else 16
    text_off = align_up(len(data), text_align)
    data += b"\x00" * (text_off - len(data))
    data += prog_bytes
    sections.append(dict(name_off=name_offsets['.text'], type=SHT_PROGBITS,
                         flags=SHF_ALLOC | SHF_EXECINSTR, addr=0, off=text_off,
                         size=len(prog_bytes), link=0, info=0, addralign=text_align,
                         entsize=0, content=prog_bytes))

    # .license
    lic = license_bytes + (b"\x00" if not license_bytes.endswith(b"\x00") else b"")
    lic_align = 1
    lic_off = align_up(len(data), lic_align)
    data += b"\x00" * (lic_off - len(data))
    data += lic
    sections.append(dict(name_off=name_offsets['.license'], type=SHT_PROGBITS,
                         flags=SHF_ALLOC, addr=0, off=lic_off, size=len(lic), link=0,
                         info=0, addralign=lic_align, entsize=0, content=lic))

    # Optional .rodata
    if extras.get('rodata') is not None:
        ro = extras['rodata']
        ro_align = rng.choice([1, 4, 8])
        ro_off = align_up(len(data), ro_align)
        data += b"\x00" * (ro_off - len(data))
        data += ro
        sections.append(dict(name_off=name_offsets['.rodata'], type=SHT_PROGBITS,
                             flags=SHF_ALLOC, addr=0, off=ro_off, size=len(ro), link=0,
                             info=0, addralign=ro_align, entsize=0, content=ro))

    # Optional .maps (empty placeholder)
    if extras.get('maps') is not None:
        mp = extras['maps']
        mp_align = 4
        mp_off = align_up(len(data), mp_align)
        data += b"\x00" * (mp_off - len(data))
        data += mp
        sections.append(dict(name_off=name_offsets['.maps'], type=SHT_PROGBITS,
                             flags=SHF_ALLOC, addr=0, off=mp_off, size=len(mp), link=0,
                             info=0, addralign=mp_align, entsize=0, content=mp))

    # .BTF
    if use_btf:
        btf_align = 4
        btf_off = align_up(len(data), btf_align)
        data += b"\x00" * (btf_off - len(data))
        data += btf_bytes
        sections.append(dict(name_off=name_offsets['.BTF'], type=SHT_PROGBITS,
                             flags=SHF_ALLOC, addr=0, off=btf_off, size=len(btf_bytes),
                             link=0, info=0, addralign=btf_align, entsize=0, content=btf_bytes))

    # .shstrtab
    shstr_align = 1
    shstr_off = align_up(len(data), shstr_align)
    data += b"\x00" * (shstr_off - len(data))
    data += shstr
    sections.append(dict(name_off=name_offsets['.shstrtab'], type=SHT_STRTAB,
                         flags=0, addr=0, off=shstr_off, size=len(shstr), link=0,
                         info=0, addralign=shstr_align, entsize=0, content=shstr))

    # Section headers
    shoff = align_up(len(data), 8)
    data += b"\x00" * (shoff - len(data))

    e_shnum = len(sections)
    e_shstrndx = len(sections) - 1

    # Patch header: e_shoff, e_shnum, e_shstrndx
    data[40:48] = struct.pack('<Q', shoff)
    data[58:60] = struct.pack('<H', e_shnum)
    data[60:62] = struct.pack('<H', e_shstrndx)

    for s in sections:
        data += struct.pack('<IIQQQQIIQQ',
                            s['name_off'], s['type'], s['flags'], s['addr'], s['off'], s['size'],
                            s['link'], s['info'], s['addralign'], s['entsize'])

    return bytes(data)


def random_license(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    choices = [
        b"GPL", b"GPLv2", b"GPLv2+", b"Dual BSD/GPL", b"MIT", b"BSD", b"Apache-2.0",
        b"(GPL-2.0-only)", b"(GPL-2.0-or-later)", b"(LGPL-2.1-only)", b"(LGPL-2.1-or-later)"
    ]
    s = rng.choice(choices)
    if rng.random() < 0.25:
        s += b" note"
    return s


def gen_extras(rng: random.Random):
    extras = {}
    # Sometimes include .rodata with small bytes
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        sz = rng.randrange(0, 32)
        ro = bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(sz))
        extras['rodata'] = ro
    else:
        extras['rodata'] = None
    # Sometimes include .maps placeholder (empty or a few bytes)
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        sz = rng.randrange(0, 16)
        mp = b"" if sz == 0 else bytes([0]) * sz
        extras['maps'] = mp
    else:
        extras['maps'] = None
    return extras


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    prog = build_prog_variant(rng)
    lic = random_license(rng)

    # Randomly include BTF 80% to add variety
    btf = build_btf_blob(rng) if rng.random() < 0.8 else None

    extras = gen_extras(rng)
    elf = build_elf(prog, lic, btf, extras, rng)

    # Keep under 4096. Our builds are small, but safeguard by dropping extras if oversized
    if len(elf) > 4096:
        extras = {'rodata': None, 'maps': None}
        btf = None
        elf = build_elf(build_prog_variant(rng), lic, btf, extras, rng)

    return elf

# Data type: filesystem path
# We generate realistic bpffs-like and general filesystem paths that libbpf APIs expect.
# Target stubs use FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME() and FUZZ_PARAM_STR() for paths and names.
# We will emit a single bytes buffer that, when consumed sequentially by the fuzzer,

    "/sys/fs/bpf",
    "/run/bpffs",
]

ELF_SUFFIXES = [".o", ".bpf.o", ".elf", ".so"]

SAFE_DIRS = [
    "/tmp",
    "/var/tmp",

]

]

    "read", "write", "socket", "connect", "accept",
]

USDT_NAMES = ["gc-start", "gc-done", "request-start", "request-done", "alloc", "free"]


def _rand_components(r: random.Random, n_min=1, n_max=4) -> List[str]:

    comps = []

        l = r.randint(1, 12)
        s = ''.join(r.choices(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_", k=l))
        comps.append(s)
    return comps

    root = r.choice(BPFFS_ROOTS)
    sub = r.choice(PIN_SUBDIRS)
    comps = _rand_components(r, 0, 3)
    base = ''.join(r.choices(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits, k=r.randint(4, 10)))
    return "/".join([root, sub] + comps + [base])


def _mk_rel_path(r: random.Random) -> str:

    suffix = r.choice(ELF_SUFFIXES)

    else:

# Generate many valid but varied minimal ELF64 little-endian eBPF (EM_BPF) objects.
# Variability knobs:
# - Optional sections (.data, .rodata, .bss, custom .note, multiple strtabs)
# - Random section ordering (while keeping index of .shstrtab tracked correctly)
# - Random alignments and sizes (including zero-length sections)
# - Random filler bytes in .text/.rodata
# - Optional extra empty SHT_NULL section headers
# - Optional section header string table contents order varies
# The output remains a valid ET_REL ELF with correct headers.

ELFDATA2LSB = 1
EV_CURRENT = 1
ET_REL = 1
EM_BPF = 247

SHT_NULL = 0
SHT_PROGBITS = 1
SHT_SYMTAB = 2
SHT_STRTAB = 3
SHT_NOBITS = 8

SHF_WRITE = 0x1
SHF_ALLOC = 0x2
SHF_EXECINSTR = 0x4

ELF64_SH_FMT = '<IIQQQQIIQQ'
ELF64_HDR_SIZE = struct.calcsize(ELF64_HDR_FMT)
ELF64_SH_SIZE = struct.calcsize(ELF64_SH_FMT)


def _build_strtab(strings: List[str]) -> Tuple[bytes, dict]:
    # Start with NUL entry
    data = bytearray(b'\x00')
    off = {"": 0}
    for s in strings:
        if s in off:
            continue
        off[s] = len(data)
        data += s.encode('utf-8') + b'\x00'
    return bytes(data), off


def _align(buf: bytearray, align: int) -> None:
    if align <= 0:
        return
    pad = (-len(buf)) % align
    if pad:
        buf += b'\x00' * pad


def _rand_bytes(r: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    if n <= 0:
        return b''
    # Bias towards zeroes with some randomness to keep mostly benign data
    return bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def _make_sections(r: random.Random) -> List[Tuple[str, int, int, int]]:
    # Define candidate sections with (name, type, flags, align)
    sects = []
    # .text must exist
    text_align = 1 << r.randrange(0, 3)  # 1,2,4
    sects.append((".text", SHT_PROGBITS, SHF_ALLOC | SHF_EXECINSTR, max(1, text_align)))

    # Optionals
    if r.random() < 0.8:
        ro_align = 1 << r.randrange(0, 4)  # 1,2,4,8
        sects.append((".rodata", SHT_PROGBITS, SHF_ALLOC, max(1, ro_align)))
    if r.random() < 0.6:
        data_align = 1 << r.randrange(0, 4)
        sects.append((".data", SHT_PROGBITS, SHF_ALLOC | SHF_WRITE, max(1, data_align)))
    if r.random() < 0.5:

        sects.append((".bss", SHT_NOBITS, SHF_ALLOC | SHF_WRITE, max(1, bss_align)))
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        note_align = 4
        sects.append((".note.gnu.build-id", SHT_PROGBITS, 0, note_align))

    # Shuffle order to vary sh_name offsets and layout; .text should remain present somewhere
    r.shuffle(sects)
    return sects

            # Small executable bytes; can be empty too
            size = r.randrange(0, 32)
            sect_contents[name] = _rand_bytes(r, size)
        elif shtype == SHT_NOBITS:
            # .bss: NOBITS, choose size but no bytes emitted
            size = r.randrange(0, 64)
            sect_contents[name] = b"\x00" * 0  # not stored, only size used
            # store size in a side map via length of empty content is 0; size tracked separately below
        else:
            maxlen = 64 if name == ".rodata" else 48
            size = r.randrange(0, maxlen)
            sect_contents[name] = _rand_bytes(r, size)

    # Randomly add extra SHT_NULL headers for variability
    extra_null_sh = r.randrange(0, 3)

    # Layout: [ELF header][SH table][section data blobs (for PROGBITS/STR)]; NOBITS has size but no data
    file = bytearray(b"\x00" * ELF64_HDR_SIZE)

    # Precompute section header count: 1 null + shstrtab + strtab + defined + extras
    sh_entries = 1 + 2 + len(sect_defs) + extra_null_sh

    shoff = len(file)
    file += b"\x00" * (ELF64_SH_SIZE * sh_entries)

    # Append .shstrtab data
    _align(file, 1)
    shstrtab_off = len(file)
    file += shstr_blob

    # Append .strtab data
    _align(file, 1)
    strtab_off = len(file)
    file += strtab_blob

    # Append each section content and record header fields
    sections = []  # (name, type, flags, addr, off, size, link, info, align, entsize)

    # 0: NULL
    sections.append(("", SHT_NULL, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0))

    # .shstrtab
    sections.append((".shstrtab", SHT_STRTAB, 0, 0, shstrtab_off, len(shstr_blob), 0, 0, 1, 0))

    # .strtab
    sections.append((".strtab", SHT_STRTAB, 0, 0, strtab_off, len(strtab_blob), 0, 0, 1, 0))

    # Materialize defined sections
    for name, shtype, flags, align in sect_defs:
        if shtype == SHT_NOBITS:
            # NOBITS: reserve no data, but record size
            size = r.randrange(0, 64)
            _align(file, max(1, align))
            off = len(file)  # conventionally offset can be where it would be, but for NOBITS it is ignored by loader
            sections.append((name, shtype, flags, 0, off, size, 0, 0, max(1, align), 0))
        else:
            blob = sect_contents.get(name, b"")
            _align(file, max(1, align))
            off = len(file)
            file += blob
            sections.append((name, shtype, flags, 0, off, len(blob), 0, 0, max(1, align), 0))

    # Add extra NULL section headers to vary counts (at end)
    for _ in range(extra_null_sh):
        sections.append(("", SHT_NULL, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0))

    # Build section header table
    def sh_name_index(nm: str) -> int:
        return shstr_off.get(nm, 0)

    sh_table = bytearray()
    for name, shtype, flags, addr, off, size, link, info, addralign, entsize in sections:
        sh_table += struct.pack(
            ELF64_SH_FMT,
            sh_name_index(name),
            shtype,
            flags,
            addr,
            off,
            size,
            link,
            info,
            addralign,
            entsize,
        )

    # Patch SH table
    file[shoff:shoff + len(sh_table)] = sh_table

    # ELF header
    e_ident = bytearray(16)
    e_ident[0:4] = b'\x7fELF'
    e_ident[4] = ELFCLASS64
    e_ident[5] = ELFDATA2LSB
    e_ident[6] = EV_CURRENT

    e_type = ET_REL
    e_machine = EM_BPF
    e_version = EV_CURRENT
    e_entry = 0
    e_phoff = 0
    e_shoff = shoff
    e_flags = 0
    e_ehsize = ELF64_HDR_SIZE
    e_phentsize = 0
    e_phnum = 0
    e_shentsize = ELF64_SH_SIZE
    e_shnum = len(sections)
    # Find index of .shstrtab in our sections list
    shstrndx = 0
    for idx, (nm, *_rest) in enumerate(sections):
        if nm == ".shstrtab":
            shstrndx = idx
            break

    elf_hdr = struct.pack(
        ELF64_HDR_FMT,
        bytes(e_ident),
        e_type,
        e_machine,
        e_version,
        e_entry,
        e_phoff,
        e_shoff,
        e_flags,
        e_ehsize,
        e_phentsize,
        e_phnum,
        e_shentsize,
        e_shnum,
        shstrndx,
    )

    file[0:ELF64_HDR_SIZE] = elf_hdr

    return bytes(file)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    # Introduce additional variability by mixing the seed with a few internal draws
    mixed = (seed * 1103515245 + 12345 + r.getrandbits(16)) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    blob = _emit_elf(mixed)
    if len(blob) > 4096:
        blob = blob[:4096]
    return blob

import os
import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator aims to produce a single bytes buffer that, when split by the
# harness into FUZZ_PARAM_STR and FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME consumables, yields
# valid, interesting inputs for:
# - bpf_object__open_file: needs a valid ELF path (filename) and some
#   alphanumeric-ish strings for object_name and pin_root_path.
# - Various BTF mutation calls expecting NUL-terminated strings (names, tags).
# - tc hook paths (qdisc string) and other general strings.
#
# Strategy
# - Emit a small virtual file set encoded into the buffer: one primary file
#   path followed by file contents (an ELF header + minimal section stubs),
#   then a sequence of NUL-terminated strings suitable for names.
# - The fuzzer infra typically maps FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME to a file extracted
#   from the buffer and FUZZ_PARAM_STR to strings parsed from the same buffer.
# - Keep sizes <= 4096 bytes.
#
# We craft:
# 1) A NUL-terminated filename like "/tmp/fuzz.o" (path-like, simple).
# 2) A length-prefixed blob that represents the file contents. We’ll provide a
#    valid ELF64 little-endian header with minimal plausible fields so that
#    libbpf can attempt to parse it as a BPF ELF (even if later stages may
#    fail gracefully). We include an eBPF section name ".BTF" and ".text"
#    markers in the string table to increase acceptance likelihood.
# 3) A set of NUL-terminated alphanumeric strings for object_name, pin_root_path,
#    qdisc, and many BTF names (identifiers, enum names, etc.).
#
# Note: We do not rely on the harness’s exact parsing rules, but providing a
# single buffer with multiple NUL-terminated strings and a file blob is a
# common pattern for such fuzzers.

ELF_MAGIC = b"\x7fELF"

def rand_ident(rng: random.Random, min_len=3, max_len=12) -> str:
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_"
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Ensure first char is letter or underscore for nicer identifiers
    first = rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + "_")
    rest = ''.join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n - 1))
    return first + rest

def rand_path(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Provide a plausible bpffs or tmp path; libbpf open_file just needs a filesystem path
    bases = ["/tmp", "/var/tmp", "/dev/shm", "/tmp/bpf", "/sys/fs/bpf"]
    base = rng.choice(bases)
    name = rand_ident(rng, 4, 10)
    ext = rng.choice([".o", ".elf", ".obj"])  # object-like
    return f"{base}/{name}{ext}"

def build_min_elf64_bpf(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Construct a minimal ELF64 little-endian object with a couple of sections.
    # It won't be a fully functional BPF object, but aims to be well-formed
    # enough for initial parsing.
    # ELF64 Header (64 bytes)
    e_ident = bytearray(16)
    e_ident[0:4] = ELF_MAGIC         # 0x7f 'E' 'L' 'F'
    e_ident[4] = 2                   # EI_CLASS = ELFCLASS64
    e_ident[5] = 1                   # EI_DATA = ELFDATA2LSB
    e_ident[6] = 1                   # EI_VERSION = EV_CURRENT
    e_ident[7] = 0                   # EI_OSABI = SYSV
    # rest zeros

    def u16(x):
        return x.to_bytes(2, 'little')
    def u32(x):
        return x.to_bytes(4, 'little')
    def u64(x):
        return x.to_bytes(8, 'little')

    e_type = u16(1)                  # ET_REL
    e_machine = u16(247)             # EM_BPF (0xF7)
    e_version = u32(1)
    e_entry = u64(0)
    e_phoff = u64(0)
    e_shoff = u64(0)  # to be filled later
    e_flags = u32(0)
    e_ehsize = u16(64)
    e_phentsize = u16(0)
    e_phnum = u16(0)
    e_shentsize = u16(64)            # sizeof(Elf64_Shdr)
    e_shnum = u16(0)                 # to fill
    e_shstrndx = u16(0)              # to fill

    ehdr = bytes(e_ident) + e_type + e_machine + e_version + e_entry + e_phoff + e_shoff + e_flags + e_ehsize + e_phentsize + e_phnum + e_shentsize + e_shnum + e_shstrndx

    # Build sections: we will have section 0 (NULL), .text, .BTF, .strtab, .symtab, .shstrtab
    # Create string table for section names (.shstrtab)
    shstr = bytearray()
    def add_shstr(s: str) -> int:
        off = len(shstr)
        shstr.extend(s.encode('utf-8') + b"\x00")
        return off
    shstr.extend(b"\x00")  # index 0 empty
    off_text = add_shstr(".text")
    off_btf = add_shstr(".BTF")
    off_strtab = add_shstr(".strtab")
    off_symtab = add_shstr(".symtab")
    off_shstrtab = add_shstr(".shstrtab")

    # Create .text with a small NOP-like BPF insn bytes (8 bytes per insn). We'll place a single exit insn 0x95 00 00 00 00 00 00 00
    text = bytes([0x95,0,0,0,0,0,0,0])
    # Create minimal .BTF blob header to look plausible (not necessarily fully valid)
    # BTF header: magic 0xeb9f, version=1, flags=0, hdr_len=24, type_off/len, str_off/len
    btf_hdr = b"\x9f\xeb" + b"\x01\x00" + u32(0) + u32(24) + u32(0) + u32(0) + u32(0) + u32(4)
    btf_strs = b"\x00bpf\x00"
    btf = btf_hdr + btf_strs
    # .strtab (for symbols) minimal
    strtab = b"\x00" + b"prog\x00"
    # .symtab: create a single symbol for .text
    # Elf64_Sym: st_name, st_info, st_other, st_shndx, st_value, st_size
    st_name = (1).to_bytes(4,'little')  # points to "prog"
    st_info = bytes([0x12])  # STB_GLOBAL + STT_FUNC
    st_other = b"\x00"
    st_shndx = (1).to_bytes(2,'little') # .text index later (we will set to 1 as we plan)
    st_value = u64(0)
    st_size = u64(len(text))
    symtab = st_name + st_info + st_other + st_shndx + st_value + st_size

    # Helper to build section header
    SHT_NULL=0; SHT_PROGBITS=1; SHT_SYMTAB=2; SHT_STRTAB=3
    SHF_ALLOC=2; SHF_EXECINSTR=4

    shdrs = []
    data_segments = []

    # placeholder for alignment/padding
    def align(cur, a):
        rem = cur % a
        return 0 if rem==0 else (a - rem)

    # Section 0 NULL
    shdrs.append(dict(name=0, type=SHT_NULL, flags=0, addr=0, off=0, size=0, link=0, info=0, addralign=0, entsize=0))

    # .text = index 1
    shdrs.append(dict(name=off_text, type=SHT_PROGBITS, flags=SHF_ALLOC|SHF_EXECINSTR, addr=0, off=0, size=len(text), link=0, info=0, addralign=8, entsize=0))
    data_segments.append((1, text, 8))

    # .BTF = index 2
    shdrs.append(dict(name=off_btf, type=SHT_PROGBITS, flags=0, addr=0, off=0, size=len(btf), link=0, info=0, addralign=4, entsize=0))
    data_segments.append((2, btf, 4))

    # .strtab = index 3
    shdrs.append(dict(name=off_strtab, type=SHT_STRTAB, flags=0, addr=0, off=0, size=len(strtab), link=0, info=0, addralign=1, entsize=0))
    data_segments.append((3, strtab, 1))

    # .symtab = index 4
    entsize_sym = 24
    shdrs.append(dict(name=off_symtab, type=SHT_SYMTAB, flags=0, addr=0, off=0, size=len(symtab), link=3, info=0, addralign=8, entsize=entsize_sym))
    data_segments.append((4, symtab, 8))

    # .shstrtab = index 5
    shstr_bytes = bytes(shstr)
    shdrs.append(dict(name=off_shstrtab, type=SHT_STRTAB, flags=0, addr=0, off=0, size=len(shstr_bytes), link=0, info=0, addralign=1, entsize=0))
    data_segments.append((5, shstr_bytes, 1))

    # Now layout: [ehdr][...data...][shdr table]
    cur = len(ehdr)
    blob = bytearray(ehdr)

    # place each data segment with alignment and record offset/size
    for idx, data, al in data_segments:
        pad = align(cur, al)
        if pad:
            blob.extend(b"\x00" * pad)
            cur += pad
        shdrs[idx]["off"] = cur
        shdrs[idx]["size"] = len(data)
        blob.extend(data)
        cur += len(data)

    # align for section headers (8)
    pad = (8 - (cur % 8)) % 8
    if pad:
        blob.extend(b"\x00" * pad)
        cur += pad

    e_shoff_val = cur
    e_shnum_val = len(shdrs)
    e_shstrndx_val = 5

    # Append section header table
    def shdr_bytes(h):
        return (
            u32(h["name"]) +
            u32(h["type"]) +
            u64(h["flags"]) +
            u64(h["addr"]) +
            u64(h["off"]) +
            u64(h["size"]) +
            u32(h["link"]) +
            u32(h["info"]) +
            u64(h["addralign"]) +
            u64(h["entsize"]) )

    for h in shdrs:
        blob.extend(shdr_bytes(h))
    cur += 64 * len(shdrs)

    # Patch e_shoff/e_shnum/e_shstrndx
    # e_shoff at byte offset 40 in ELF64 header; e_shnum at 60; e_shstrndx at 62
    def patch(offset, b):
        blob[offset:offset+len(b)] = b
    patch(40, u64(e_shoff_val))
    patch(58, u16(e_shnum_val))
    patch(60, u16(e_shstrndx_val))

    return bytes(blob)


def build_strings_block(rng: random.Random, count: int) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    # Include some common names used by BTF and libbpf
    seeds = [
        "xdp", "tracepoint", "kprobe", "uprobe", "perf", "lsm",
        ".text", ".BTF", "data", "rodata", "bss",
        "fentry", "fexit", "tc", "qdisc", "clsact",
        "fuzzprog", "my_map", "my_prog", "provider", "usdt_evt"
    ]
    rng.shuffle(seeds)
    for s in seeds[:min(len(seeds), max(0, count//3))]:
        out.extend(s.encode('utf-8') + b"\x00")
    # Then add random identifiers
    for _ in range(count):
        s = rand_ident(rng)
        out.extend(s.encode('utf-8') + b"\x00")
    return bytes(out)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Filename path
    path = rand_path(rng)
    path_bytes = path.encode('utf-8') + b"\x00"

    # ELF object contents
    elf = build_min_elf64_bpf(rng)

    # Simple header to describe a file blob for the harness (length prefix), followed by data
    # Format: b"FILE\x00" <u32 len> <bytes>
    file_tag = b"FILE\x00"
    elf_len = len(elf).to_bytes(4, 'little')

    # Alphanumeric strings block for FUZZ_PARAM_STR uses
    strs = build_strings_block(rng, count=30)

    # Optionally include a plausible pin root path and object name near the beginning as NUL strings
    pin_root = rng.choice(["/sys/fs/bpf", "/sys/fs/bpf/fuzz", "/sys/fs/bpf/test"]).encode('utf-8') + b"\x00"
    obj_name = rand_ident(rng, 4, 12).encode('utf-8') + b"\x00"

    # Compose final buffer
    # [filename NUL][pin_root NUL][object_name NUL]["FILE\0"][u32 size][ELF][strings...]
    buf = bytearray()
    buf.extend(path_bytes)
    buf.extend(pin_root)
    buf.extend(obj_name)
    buf.extend(file_tag)
    buf.extend(elf_len)
    buf.extend(elf)
    buf.extend(strs)

    # Cap to 4096 bytes
    return bytes(buf[:4096])

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator produces identifier-like strings suitable for libbpf/libbpf-based
# APIs used in the fuzz stubs. It aims to generate valid-looking names across
# multiple domains: section names, attach types, kernel symbols, syscalls,
# tracepoint categories/names, USDT provider/probe names, and file-like paths
# for FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME.
#
# The harness uses FUZZ_PARAM_STR() and FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME(). We provide a single
# bytes buffer; typical fuzzing frameworks split this buffer to satisfy multiple
# FUZZ_PARAM_* calls. To maximize usefulness, the buffer is a concatenation of
# newline-separated candidate strings, with the first line often being a strong
# candidate (valid/known). Subsequent lines include additional variations.
#
# Limit total size to <= 4096 bytes as requested.

# Some curated known-good sets to increase odds of successful API paths.
KNOWN_SECTIONS = [
    # Common SEC() names recognized by libbpf
    "xdp", "tc", "sockops", "sk_skb", "kprobe", "kretprobe", "uprobe", "uretprobe",
    "tracepoint", "raw_tracepoint", "raw_tp", "tp_btf", "lsm", "iter", "fentry",
    "fexit", "fmod_ret", "freplace",
]

KNOWN_ATTACH_TYPES = [
    # Names accepted by libbpf_attach_type_by_name/libbpf_prog_type_by_name mappings
    "xdp", "tp_btf", "tracepoint", "raw_tracepoint", "kprobe", "kretprobe", "uprobe",
    "uretprobe", "cgroup_skb", "cgroup_sock", "cgroup_sock_addr", "lsm", "perf_event",
]

KNOWN_SYSCALLS = [
    "bpf", "openat", "close", "read", "write", "mmap", "munmap", "clone", "fork",
    "execve", "ioctl", "socket", "connect", "accept", "bind", "listen",
]

# Common kernel tracepoint categories and names
TP_CATEGORIES = {
    "sched": ["sched_switch", "sched_wakeup", "sched_waking"],
    "net": ["net_dev_queue", "netif_receive_skb", "net_dev_xmit"],
    "block": ["block_rq_issue", "block_rq_complete"],
    "irq": ["irq_handler_entry", "irq_handler_exit"],
    "syscalls": [
        "sys_enter_openat", "sys_exit_openat", "sys_enter_bpf", "sys_exit_bpf"
    ],
}

# Some realistic kernel symbol/function name stems
KSYM_PREFIXES = ["__", "_", "" ]
KFUNC_BASES = [
    "do_sys_openat2", "security_bpf", "tcp_v4_connect", "do_exit", "sched_yield",
    "kmem_cache_alloc", "kmalloc", "kfree", "copy_from_user", "copy_to_user",
]

# USDT provider/probe examples (generic)
USDT_PROVIDERS = ["ruby", "python", "node", "postgresql", "java", "golang"]
USDT_PROBES = ["method__entry", "method__return", "gc__start", "gc__done", "query__start", "query__done"]

# Reasonable binary paths for uprobes/USDT
BINARY_PATHS = [
    "/bin/bash", "/bin/ls", "/usr/bin/python3", "/usr/bin/node", "/usr/bin/ruby",
    "/usr/bin/grep", "/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6", "/proc/self/exe"
]

ALNUM = string.ascii_letters + string.digits
IDENT_EXTRA = "_:."  # allow colon/dot for category:name or section.sub


def _rand_ident(rng: random.Random, min_len=1, max_len=24, allow_extra=True) -> str:
    first_chars = string.ascii_letters + "_"
    rest_chars = first_chars + string.digits
    if allow_extra:
        rest_chars += IDENT_EXTRA
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    if n <= 0:
        n = 1
    s = [rng.choice(first_chars)]
    for _ in range(n - 1):
        s.append(rng.choice(rest_chars))
    return "".join(s)


def _maybe_with_subsec(rng: random.Random, base: str) -> str:
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        return base
    # Add a suffix like /foo or /bar to mimic SEC("tracepoint/syscalls") etc.
    sep = "/" if rng.random() < 0.7 else "+"
    return base + sep + _rand_ident(rng, 3, 10, allow_extra=False)


def _build_tracepoint_pair(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    # Returns [category, name]
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        cat = rng.choice(list(TP_CATEGORIES.keys()))
        name = rng.choice(TP_CATEGORIES[cat])
        return [cat, name]
    # random fallback
    return [_rand_ident(rng, 3, 10, allow_extra=False), _rand_ident(rng, 3, 16, allow_extra=False)]


def _build_kernel_symbol(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        return rng.choice(KSYM_PREFIXES) + rng.choice(KFUNC_BASES)
    # random symbol-like
    return _rand_ident(rng, 4, 24, allow_extra=False)


def _build_attach_type_name(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        return rng.choice(KNOWN_ATTACH_TYPES)
    return _rand_ident(rng, 3, 14, allow_extra=False)


def _build_section_name(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    base = rng.choice(KNOWN_SECTIONS) if rng.random() < 0.7 else _rand_ident(rng, 3, 12, allow_extra=False)
    return _maybe_with_subsec(rng, base)


def _build_syscall_name(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    return rng.choice(KNOWN_SYSCALLS) if rng.random() < 0.7 else _rand_ident(rng, 2, 12, allow_extra=False)


def _build_usdt_names(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    provider = rng.choice(USDT_PROVIDERS) if rng.random() < 0.6 else _rand_ident(rng, 3, 12, allow_extra=False)
    probe = rng.choice(USDT_PROBES) if rng.random() < 0.6 else _rand_ident(rng, 3, 18, allow_extra=False)
    return [provider, probe]


def _build_binary_path(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    if rng.random() < 0.75:
        return rng.choice(BINARY_PATHS)
    # Construct a plausible absolute path
    parts = ["/"]
    depth = rng.randint(1, 4)
    for _ in range(depth):
        parts.append(_rand_ident(rng, 2, 10, allow_extra=False))
    # file name with optional extension
    fname = _rand_ident(rng, 2, 12, allow_extra=False)
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        ext = rng.choice([".so", ".so.6", ".bin", ".exe", ".py"])  # harmless extensions
        fname += ext
    parts.append(fname)
    # join
    p = "/".join([p for p in parts if p != "/"])  # avoid double slashes
    return "/" + p


def _assemble_lines(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    lines: List[str] = []

    # 1) A good section name and variants
    lines.append(_build_section_name(rng))
    lines.append(_build_section_name(rng))

    # 2) Attach type names
    lines.append(_build_attach_type_name(rng))
    lines.append(_build_attach_type_name(rng))

    # 3) Kernel symbol candidates for kprobe
    lines.append(_build_kernel_symbol(rng))
    lines.append(_build_kernel_symbol(rng))

    # 4) Syscall names
    lines.append(_build_syscall_name(rng))

    # 5) Tracepoint category and name (two separate strings expected by some stubs)
    cat, name = _build_tracepoint_pair(rng)
    lines.append(cat)
    lines.append(name)

    # 6) Raw tracepoint name (e.g., sched_switch without category)
    lines.append(name if rng.random() < 0.5 else _rand_ident(rng, 4, 16, allow_extra=False))

    # 7) USDT provider/name
    provider, probe = _build_usdt_names(rng)
    lines.append(provider)
    lines.append(probe)

    # 8) Uprobe filename-like path
    lines.append(_build_binary_path(rng))

    # 9) Additional generic identifiers to satisfy extra FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls
    for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 8)):
        lines.append(_rand_ident(rng, 3, 20, allow_extra=True))

    # Ensure non-empty and deduplicate excessive empties
    lines = [s if s else "x" for s in lines]
    return lines


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    lines = _assemble_lines(rng)
    # Join with newlines so the harness can split or consume sequentially.
    blob = "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
    data = blob.encode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]
    return data

import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List

# Generator for a generic binary blob, but tailored to libbpf fuzz stubs that
# use FUZZ_PARAM_STR to feed:
# - bpf_prog_test_run_opts.data_in (<=512 bytes)
# - bpf_prog_test_run_opts.ctx_in (<=256 bytes)
# - btf__new / btf__new_split raw BTF blobs (ideally valid/minimally valid)
# - btf_ext__new raw .BTF.ext blobs (ideally valid/minimally valid)
#
# Strategy:
# We build a concatenated buffer containing a small "envelope" that encodes a
# sequence of chunks. Each chunk is prefixed with a one-byte type tag and a
# 16-bit length (little-endian), followed by that many bytes of payload.
# The fuzz harness pulls FUZZ_PARAM_STR multiple times; typical engines consume
# from the provided initial buffer sequentially. By packing several varied
# chunks we increase chances that different calls receive different useful data.
#
# Chunk types:
#  - 0x01: random ASCII payload (good for data_in/context)
#  - 0x02: random binary payload (mixed entropy)
#  - 0x03: minimally valid BTF blob
#  - 0x04: minimally valid BTF.ext blob aligned to expectations
#  - 0x05: repeated pattern bytes (edge cases: all-zero, all-FF, etc.)
#
# Minimal BTF/BTF.ext construction follows the on-disk BTF format:
#   struct btf_header {
#     __u16 magic;    # 0xeb9f (little)
#     __u8  version;  # 1
#     __u8  flags;    # 0
#     __u32 hdr_len;  # 24
#     __u32 type_off; __u32 type_len;
#     __u32 str_off;  __u32 str_len;
#   }
# We emit just a string section with "\0int\0" and zero type section (valid empty types is acceptable to parsers).
# For .BTF.ext header we follow the same header but encode ext magic 0xdecf and include an empty section with a valid
# string table. Many consumers accept an empty ext.
#
# Sizes are kept <= 1024 for BTF, and other chunks small to fit harness limits.

BTF_MAGIC = 0xEB9F
BTF_EXT_MAGIC = 0xDEC1  # Linux uses 0xDEC1 (BTF_EXT_MAGIC)
BTF_VERSION = 1
BTF_HDR_LEN = 24


def _le16(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('<H', x)


def _le32(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('<I', x)


def build_min_btf(strings: List[str]) -> bytes:
    # Build a minimal BTF with only a string section.
    # String table must start with NUL.
    uniq = ['']
    for s in strings:
        if s not in uniq:
            uniq.append(s)
    strtab = b''.join((s.encode('ascii', 'ignore') + b'\x00') for s in uniq)
    # Align to 4 bytes
    if len(strtab) % 4:
        strtab += b'\x00' * (4 - (len(strtab) % 4))

    type_off = 0
    type_len = 0
    str_off = type_off + type_len
    str_len = len(strtab)

    hdr = b''.join([
        _le16(BTF_MAGIC),
        struct.pack('<B', BTF_VERSION),
        struct.pack('<B', 0),  # flags
        _le32(BTF_HDR_LEN),
        _le32(type_off), _le32(type_len),
        _le32(str_off), _le32(str_len),
    ])
    return hdr + (b'' if type_len == 0 else b'') + strtab


def build_min_btf_ext() -> bytes:
    # Minimal BTF.ext with empty sections is acceptable to many readers.
    # Use same header layout as BTF with different magic.
    strtab = b'\x00'  # just NUL
    if len(strtab) % 4:
        strtab += b'\x00' * (4 - (len(strtab) % 4))

    type_off = 0
    type_len = 0
    str_off = type_off + type_len
    str_len = len(strtab)

    hdr = b''.join([
        _le16(BTF_EXT_MAGIC),
        struct.pack('<B', BTF_VERSION),
        struct.pack('<B', 0),
        _le32(BTF_HDR_LEN),
        _le32(type_off), _le32(type_len),
        _le32(str_off), _le32(str_len),
    ])
    return hdr + strtab


def _rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    alphabet = ''.join([
        ''.join(chr(c) for c in range(ord('a'), ord('z')+1)),
        ''.join(chr(c) for c in range(ord('A'), ord('Z')+1)),
        ''.join(chr(c) for c in range(ord('0'), ord('9')+1)),
        ' _:-./\n\t']
    )
    return ''.join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n)).encode('ascii')


def _rand_binary(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def _pattern_bytes(kind: int, n: int) -> bytes:
    if kind == 0:
        return b'\x00' * n
    if kind == 1:
        return b'\xff' * n
    if kind == 2:
        return (b'\x00\xff') * (n // 2) + (b'\x00' if n % 2 else b'')
    if kind == 3:
        return b'AB' * (n // 2) + (b'A' if n % 2 else b'')
    return bytes((i % 256 for i in range(n)))


def _emit_chunk(tag: int, payload: bytes) -> bytes:
    # length is 16-bit; cap to 65535 though we will keep well below.
    ln = min(len(payload), 0xFFFF)
    return struct.pack('<BH', tag, ln) + payload[:ln]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    chunks: List[bytes] = []

    # 1) ASCII payloads targeting data_in (<=512) and ctx_in (<=256)
    for size in [rng.randint(0, 64), rng.randint(64, 256), rng.randint(256, 512)]:
        chunks.append(_emit_chunk(0x01, _rand_ascii(rng, size)))

    # 2) Binary payloads of varied sizes (some small, some medium)
    for size in [rng.randint(0, 64), rng.randint(32, 128), rng.randint(128, 384)]:
        chunks.append(_emit_chunk(0x02, _rand_binary(rng, size)))

    # 3) Minimal valid BTF blob (helps btf__new succeed)
    # Include common strings like "int", "char", which are harmless.
    btf_blob = build_min_btf(["int", "char", "long", "unsigned"])
    # Randomly append some padding or minor extra random tail (still valid as readers use header lengths)
    tail_len = rng.randint(0, 16)
    btf_blob += _rand_binary(rng, tail_len)
    chunks.append(_emit_chunk(0x03, btf_blob))

    # 4) Minimal BTF.ext blob
    btf_ext_blob = build_min_btf_ext()
    btf_ext_blob += _rand_binary(rng, rng.randint(0, 8))
    chunks.append(_emit_chunk(0x04, btf_ext_blob))

    # 5) Patterned edge-case payloads
    for kind in range(5):
        size = rng.randint(0, 256)
        chunks.append(_emit_chunk(0x05, _pattern_bytes(kind, size)))

    # Shuffle chunks to vary consumption order
    rng.shuffle(chunks)

    # Prepend a small magic header to aid debuggability
    header = b'LBFZ' + _le16(1)  # version 1
    out = header + b''.join(chunks)

    # Ensure we respect the 4096-byte limit
    return out[:4096]
